newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares seen quiet on U.S. market holiday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares seen quiet on U.S. market holiday.

text.p: * Brazil's BNDES to sell minority holdings in 26 firms
Brazilian stocks are seen set for a quiet session Friday as major investors are likely to be on the sidelines due to today's Independence Day holiday in the U.S., brokers said.
On Thursday, market volume shrank to 922 million reais ($861.7 million) as foreign investors scaled down their activities ahead of the July 4 holiday.
Traders noted, however, local equity funds could compensate for a lack of foreign investment and boost share prices.
The funds have been the primary driving force behind the market's recent rally.

Analysts also said they would pay attention to today's auction of minority holdings in 26 firms. Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) is due to sell stakes in different state-owned companies, including Cemig, Telebras, Petrobras, among others.
The auction will take place on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
